synopsis: Published by Underwriters Laboratories, UL 4600 specifies evidence-backed coverage for an autonomous-product safety case; its third edition is dated 17 March 2023 [f15026, f15375, f15376]. It structures an intended-use safety claim into supported subclaims and uses question lists to check completeness, but sets no performance numbers and prescribes no tests [f15378, f15379, f15377]. The booklet recommends those lists for structuring the heavy off-road collision-mitigation validation plan, including a 1.5–3-page safety-scope and top-level-claim section [f9984, f10156]. This addresses an acceptance gap: the booklet says no regulation spells out off-road automatic-braking acceptance, so a structured safety case connects simulation, physical tests and analysis to assessable claims [f15386, f15387]. However, UL 4600's applicability and simulation-acceptance provisions were not verified, and the booklet records both proponents and critics of safety cases [f15384, f15383, f10319].
